question: The effect of a drug that acts as a competitive inhibitor in an enzymatic reaction:

options.opa: It can be canceled with substrate concentrations much higher than the concentration of the inhibitor.
options.opb: It does not affect the kinetic constants of the reaction.
options.opc: The higher the concentration of the enzyme-substrate (ES) complex present, the greater.
options.opd: It consists of a reduction in the apparent metabolization constant and an increase in the rate of catalysis.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Competitive inhibitor binds to the active site of the enzyme -> competes with the substrate for binding -> reduces the rate of enzyme-substrate complex formation -> 80%
CHAIN: Competitive inhibitor can be overcome by increasing the substrate concentration -> more substrate outcompetes the inhibitor for binding to the enzyme -> restores enzyme activity -> 85%
CHAIN: Presence of competitive inhibitor does not alter the maximum velocity (Vmax) of the reaction -> Vmax remains constant -> 90%
CHAIN: Competitive inhibitor increases the apparent Michaelis constant (Km) of the reaction -> Km reflects the affinity of the enzyme for the substrate -> 85%
CHAIN: Higher concentration of the enzyme-substrate (ES) complex indicates more active enzyme-substrate interactions -> higher ES concentration correlates with increased reaction rate -> 80%
CHAIN: Competitive inhibitor reduces the apparent metabolization constant -> leads to a decrease in the rate of catalysis -> 75%
analysis: A competitive inhibitor competes with the substrate for binding to the active site of the enzyme. This type of inhibition can be overcome by increasing the concentration of the substrate, as it can outcompete the inhibitor for binding to the enzyme.
